findings.title: `forEach(async ...)` drops the deleteEvent promise and escapes the surrounding try/catch in reschedule
findings.description: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` is now `async`, and the `return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` value is discarded because `forEach` ignores callback return values. Any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of reaching the `try` block. The reschedule can complete before calendar events are deleted. The same pattern appears at `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553`. Replacing `forEach` with `for...of` (as done in `handleCancelBooking`) or `Promise.all(map(...))` would make the deletes awaited and errors catchable.

findings.title: Async `forEach` in handleCancelBooking pushes into `updatedBookings` after the handler may have moved on
findings.description: In the recurring-event branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })` performs the calendar update after an await. Nothing awaits the callbacks, so the update may finish after the response is sent, and rejections are unhandled. The sibling else-branch was correctly converted to `for...of`, so the two branches are now inconsistent.

findings.title: `appStore` entries are now Promises, which breaks any synchronous consumer
findings.description: Each entry changed from a module namespace to `import("./...")`, so `appStore[key]` is a `Promise`. Every changed call site adds `await`, but any consumer that reads `appStore[key].metadata` or similar synchronously will now get `undefined` or a type error. Those consumers are outside this diff and could not be inspected here, so they need a check. Typing the map as `Record<string, Promise<AppModule>>` would make the contract explicit.

findings.title: Unawaited `getCalendar` promise is stored in a returned object typed as a resolved Calendar
findings.description: `getCalendarCredentials` now stores `calendar = getCalendar(credential)` (a `Promise`) in the returned item. `getConnectedCalendars` awaits `item.calendar`, which works, but any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that treats `item.calendar` as `Calendar | null` will break. The item's type should say `Promise<Calendar | null>`, or the item should be built after resolving.

findings.title: Unrelated blank line added inside getCalendarCredentials
findings.description: A blank line was inserted before `return credentials.length ? credentials : [];`. It is harmless, but it is unrelated to the async conversion and adds diff noise.
